# Code Patterns

This repo uses Effect-native TypeScript for boundary-crossing, fallible,
runtime-owned, schema-owned, or service-owned code. UI-only rendering can stay
plain React, but package code, loaders, runtime setup, RPC, config, command
execution, and content validation should prefer Effect primitives.

The boundary rules in this document are lint-backed through normal
`bun run check`: portable Effect rules live under `effect/*`, Bun runtime rules
under `bun/*`, portable MDX rendering rules under `mdx/*`, and this site's
route, SEO/AEO, TanStack, typography, and design-system policies under
`site/*`.

Use `Data`, `Schema`, `Array`, `Chunk`, `HashSet`, `HashMap`, `Match`,
`Context`, `Layer`, `Config`, `Service`, `Record`, `Option`, `Result`, `Exit`,
Bun/Platform `Command`, and `ManagedRuntime` before adding ad hoc TypeScript
helpers for those concerns.

## Boundary Values

- Define package, RPC, loader, config, command, and content boundary values with
  `Schema`.
- Derive TypeScript types from schemas with `typeof Schema.Type`.
- Reuse canonical schema-derived types, branded identifiers, service tags,
  tagged errors, and constructors from the owning package.
- Do not mirror canonical fields as local primitives such as `id: string`,
  `slug: string`, `title: string`, or post metadata outside their owning schema
  or service projection.
- Decode unknown input once at an explicit package, RPC, loader, config,
  command, HTTP, provider, filesystem, or content ingress with the owning
  Effect Schema. `schemas.ts` declares codecs; it is not a runtime-boundary
  exception.
- Encode only at serialization egresses such as HTTP/RPC responses, loader
  codecs, reports, command output, persisted state, or provider requests.
- Use `Schema.TaggedClass`, `Schema.TaggedError`, `Schema.TaggedStruct`, or
  `Data.TaggedClass` when a variant crosses a boundary. Import
  `Schema.TaggedError` as lower-case `taggedError` when Ultracite's generic
  `throw-new-error` rule would otherwise mistake the Effect constructor for a
  thrown JavaScript error.

## Effects, Layers, And Services

- `service.ts` files own `Context.Service` contracts and canonical request,
  response, and error shapes.
- Production wiring belongs in `live.layer.ts` or an explicit runtime/layer
  module, not in service contract files.
- Package and service code should return `Effect` values and layers. Runtime
  execution belongs in app route loaders, runtime files, server files, scripts,
  or package boundary modules that own a process/runtime lifecycle.
- Expected failures should be tagged schema errors returned through
  `Effect.fail`, `Effect.try`, or `Effect.tryPromise`, not thrown exceptions.
  Raw `try` statements are banned by `effect/no-try-statement`, including
  `try/finally`. Use Effect/Result error handling and scoped finalisation.
- Fallible Promise APIs enter through import-aware, lint-enforced
  `Effect.tryPromise({ try, catch })` boundaries. Bare callback-form
  `Effect.tryPromise` is forbidden because it leaves rejection policy implicit.
- Raw `async`, `await`, and `new Promise` are not allowed in Effect-owned
  service/runtime scopes. External Promise APIs enter through
  `Effect.promise` or `Effect.tryPromise`; keep catch mapping inline and tagged
  at that boundary.
- `process.env` and `process.argv` reads belong in explicit config, runtime,
  main, CLI, layer, adapter, or test boundaries. `console.*`,
  `Effect.runPromise`, `BunRuntime.runMain`, and `ManagedRuntime.make` belong in
  runtime, main, CLI, layer, adapter, or test boundaries. Direct host APIs and
  provider SDKs belong in live layer, runtime, CLI, or adapter modules. Package
  logic returns typed values, tagged errors, Effects, and Layers.
- Do not call throwing `Schema` or `SchemaParser` `*Sync` codecs in production,
  including top-level constants and runtime modules. Use effectful codecs at
  ingress/egress so parse failures remain in the Effect error channel.
  Non-throwing `Result`/`Exit`/`Option` decoders are reserved for synchronous
  consumers such as loader hydration, deterministic fixtures, and tests.
- `decodeTo` and `encodeTo` are schema transformations, not runtime codec
  execution. They do not establish an ingress or egress boundary.
- Tagged errors expose schema-safe diagnostics, not `Schema.Unknown` causes.
  No tagged-error payload field may use `Schema.Unknown`. Preserve defects as
  defects, or map only safe diagnostic fields at the true adapter boundary.
- Service-contract scopes reject direct `unknown` parameter annotations and
  direct `Effect.Effect<Success, unknown, Requirements>` error positions.
  Current syntax-only enforcement does not follow aliases to prove that an
  interface is a `Context.Service` contract, infer semantic identity through
  arbitrary schema composition, or prove a decoder binding has one real use.
  Keep those cases under schema/service review until a narrow AST shape is
  demonstrated; do not add a filename loophole or a sidecar lint script.
- One-off `Effect.map`, `Effect.mapError`, `Effect.catchTag`,
  `Effect.catchAll`, `Result`, or `Exit` handling should stay inline at the
  callsite unless it becomes a real reusable boundary policy.

## Optional Values

Optional request, response, frontmatter, SEO, and loader fields should be owned
by schemas. Branch with `Option.match`, `Option.isSome`, or `Option.isNone`
when behavior depends on presence.

Keep internal absence as `Option` or schema-owned optional fields. Avoid
`Option.getOrNull`, raw `null` object properties, and `Schema.NullOr` in
internal service code unless the module is explicitly modeling an external
protocol boundary.

Do not build schema-backed objects with conditional spreads:

```ts
{
  ...(description ? { description } : {})
}
```

Fix the owning schema or construct the optional value through `Option` at the
boundary. If a field should be required, make it required in the schema instead
of repeatedly omitting it at callsites.

## Functional Composition

Use pipe-first composition when sequencing transformations or Effect programs
is clearer left-to-right. Avoid nested wrapper calls such as
`toOutput(transformInput(input))` when the same flow reads better as a pipeline.

Use named reusable operations only when they own a durable policy, cross a
package boundary, or remove meaningful repeated complexity.

Do not extract one-line mapper/adapter helpers named like `map*`, `to*`,
`decode*`, `encode*`, or `normalize*` only to pass them into `Effect.map`,
`Effect.mapError`, Schema encode/decode helpers, or RPC adapter mapping. Inline
the one-off transform or move real encode/decode behavior into the owning schema
or service contract.

## Route And Middleware Boundaries

Canonical route-owned Markdown negotiation must stay redirect-only:
`@packages/aeo` owns schema-backed Accept-only decisions and Markdown
sibling redirect targets, `@packages/effect-start` owns reusable TanStack
Start/Effect middleware adapters, and `apps/web` owns the concrete route
registry plus route-owned `.md` rendering. Do not add Markdown body rendering,
route registries, or app-specific DTO mirrors to reusable packages.

The sole allowed TanStack server-function exception is
`apps/web/src/lib/http/markdown-sibling-redirect.middleware.ts`, where
`createServerOnlyFn` fences the dynamic import of the `.server.ts` handler.
TanStack production import protection rejects a direct `runtime.server` import
through `src/start.ts`, and `site/no-unscoped-tanstack-server-functions`
prevents broader server-function usage.

Specs and implementation tasks that change route/runtime/SEO/AEO behavior must
include production and test call graphs, direct route evidence, and Browser
screenshot evidence for the affected visible route or OG surface.

## Open Graph Platform Adapters

`@packages/og` owns the schema-derived renderer request/result contracts,
`OgRenderer`, `TakumiClient`, the dependency-requiring
`OgRendererTakumiLayer`, and the composed `OgRendererNativeLive`. The native
layer provides `TakumiClientLive` through `Layer.provide`. App OG services
consume `OgRenderer`; they do not import Takumi directly or mirror package
contracts with local DTOs.

The sole generic `takumi-js` render import is
`apps/web/src/lib/deployment/cloudflare/og.layer.ts`. That file is the
Cloudflare platform adapter and owns the bundled Worker-compatible
`WebAssembly.Module`. It implements the canonical `OgRenderer` service, wraps
the Promise API with `Effect.tryPromise`, validates the result with the owning
schema, and maps the complete render/decode program once to `OgRenderError`.
Do not add generic Takumi imports to package, Bun, server, script, route, or
test code. Deep Takumi helper and native imports remain internal to the
package-owned `TakumiClientLive` adapter.

Keep app OG asset, render-data, and output values schema-derived. Service
contracts may name Effect operations over those canonical types, while pure
React component props and inferred visual constants may remain TypeScript-only.
Do not add route-local error mirrors: the HTTP boundary handles canonical post,
asset, schema, and render error tags directly.

## Frontend Route Composition

Routes own their visible layout tree. Compose `PageShell`, `PageHeader`,
`PageSection`, `ProsePage`, `IndexFeed`, `MetadataRow`, and `RouteErrorBlock`
as high in the route file as possible instead of hiding complete page bodies in
route component values named `*Page`. Use route-owned `*Route` component names
when TanStack needs a component function.

Use explicit `gap-*` rhythm in primitives and route layouts. Do not introduce
`space-x-*` or `space-y-*`; those utilities couple spacing to child order and
are harder to audit across route-owned layouts.

Browser-mode route component tests should exercise TanStack Router behavior:
render through `RouterProvider` with `createMemoryHistory`, keep route
components private to their route files, and use route-owned `Link` markup.
When the full generated route tree would import server-only modules, build a
narrow test route tree from the exported route objects and the same UI
providers required by production.

## Material triggers

Require an impact ledger when a slice changes any of:

- a root/package command, manifest export, source condition, generated file, or
  package/app boundary;
- a route, loader, middleware, visible React state, route/feature workflow
  boundary, URL state, metadata, OG, SEO/AEO, or machine-readable sibling;
- an Effect Schema, branded identifier, Context service, Layer, RPC/HTTP API,
  provider client boundary, Config, tagged error, or runtime composition;
- lint/format/type/test/build/Knip/Turbo policy or a workflow edge;
- a deterministic test fixture, package/root export, manifest, source condition,
  generated output, lifecycle route, release/rollback procedure, or critical
  journey;
- Alchemy/Cloudflare desired topology, cache behavior, deployment boundary,
  identity/authority, secret name, environment, or repeatable operation;
- architecture, standards, README consumer contract, skill, runbook, proof,
  evidence, SPEC/task, or lifecycle routing.

For a mechanical refactor with no observable contract or durable-owner change,
retain an evidenced `N/A` ledger rather than forcing prose churn.

## Exact checks

Run the smallest owning checks during the slice. At closeout run:

```sh
bun run docs:check
bun run test:skills
bun run verification
git diff --check
```

When the documentation policy itself changes, also run:

```sh
bun --filter @packages/scripts test:documentation
```

Add affected package typechecks/tests/builds and direct browser/HTTP/provider
readbacks only when the claim requires them and authority permits them. Local
docs and skill checks never prove hosted CI, preview, production, deployment,
release, public behavior, or provider actuality.

## Package and README contract

Every workspace package and app keeps one concise README that states its owned
capability, public boundary/exports, supported local commands, and pointer to
the relevant architecture owner. Do not copy live provider values, full
runbooks, code tutorials, or cross-repository policy into READMEs.

## Lifecycle and retention

Keep only genuinely current work under active routes. Implemented/historical
SPECs and completed plans remain reachable outside default context. A
superseded or tombstone document names a current successor and reason. Preserve
failed/inconclusive outcome and provenance without surfacing raw experiments in
the default context. Do not move or delete screenshots, HAR files, transcripts,
JSON receipts, or other raw evidence without an approved retention manifest.

# Code Patterns

This repo uses Effect-native TypeScript for boundary-crossing, fallible,
runtime-owned, schema-owned, or service-owned code. UI-only rendering can stay
plain React, but package code, loaders, runtime setup, RPC, config, command
execution, and content validation should prefer Effect primitives.

The boundary rules in this document are lint-backed through normal
`bun run check`: portable Effect rules live under `effect/*`, Bun runtime rules
under `bun/*`, portable MDX rendering rules under `mdx/*`, and this site's
route, SEO/AEO, TanStack, typography, and design-system policies under
`site/*`.

Use `Data`, `Schema`, `Array`, `Chunk`, `HashSet`, `HashMap`, `Match`,
`Context`, `Layer`, `Config`, `Service`, `Record`, `Option`, `Result`, `Exit`,
Bun/Platform `Command`, and `ManagedRuntime` before adding ad hoc TypeScript
helpers for those concerns.

## Boundary Values

- Define package, RPC, loader, config, command, and content boundary values with
  `Schema`.
- Derive TypeScript types from schemas with `typeof Schema.Type`.
- Reuse canonical schema-derived types, branded identifiers, service tags,
  tagged errors, and constructors from the owning package.
- Do not mirror canonical fields as local primitives such as `id: string`,
  `slug: string`, `title: string`, or post metadata outside their owning schema
  or service projection.
- Decode unknown input once at an explicit package, RPC, loader, config,
  command, HTTP, provider, filesystem, or content ingress with the owning
  Effect Schema. `schemas.ts` declares codecs; it is not a runtime-boundary
  exception.
- Encode only at serialization egresses such as HTTP/RPC responses, loader
  codecs, reports, command output, persisted state, or provider requests.
- Use `Schema.TaggedClass`, `Schema.TaggedError`, `Schema.TaggedStruct`, or
  `Data.TaggedClass` when a variant crosses a boundary. Import
  `Schema.TaggedError` as lower-case `taggedError` when Ultracite's generic
  `throw-new-error` rule would otherwise mistake the Effect constructor for a
  thrown JavaScript error.

## Effects, Layers, And Services

- `service.ts` files own `Context.Service` contracts and canonical request,
  response, and error shapes.
- Production wiring belongs in `live.layer.ts` or an explicit runtime/layer
  module, not in service contract files.
- Package and service code should return `Effect` values and layers. Runtime
  execution belongs in app route loaders, runtime files, server files, scripts,
  or package boundary modules that own a process/runtime lifecycle.
- Expected failures should be tagged schema errors returned through
  `Effect.fail`, `Effect.try`, or `Effect.tryPromise`, not thrown exceptions.
  Raw `try` statements are banned by `effect/no-try-statement`, including
  `try/finally`. Use Effect/Result error handling and scoped finalisation.
- Fallible Promise APIs enter through import-aware, lint-enforced
  `Effect.tryPromise({ try, catch })` boundaries. Bare callback-form
  `Effect.tryPromise` is forbidden because it leaves rejection policy implicit.
- Raw `async`, `await`, and `new Promise` are not allowed in Effect-owned
  service/runtime scopes. External Promise APIs enter through
  `Effect.promise` or `Effect.tryPromise`; keep catch mapping inline and tagged
  at that boundary.
- `process.env` and `process.argv` reads belong in explicit config, runtime,
  main, CLI, layer, adapter, or test boundaries. `console.*`,
  `Effect.runPromise`, `BunRuntime.runMain`, and `ManagedRuntime.make` belong in
  runtime, main, CLI, layer, adapter, or test boundaries. Direct host APIs and
  provider SDKs belong in live layer, runtime, CLI, or adapter modules. Package
  logic returns typed values, tagged errors, Effects, and Layers.
- Do not call throwing `Schema` or `SchemaParser` `*Sync` codecs in production,
  including top-level constants and runtime modules. Use effectful codecs at
  ingress/egress so parse failures remain in the Effect error channel.
  Non-throwing `Result`/`Exit`/`Option` decoders are reserved for synchronous
  consumers such as loader hydration, deterministic fixtures, and tests.
- `decodeTo` and `encodeTo` are schema transformations, not runtime codec
  execution. They do not establish an ingress or egress boundary.
- Tagged errors expose schema-safe diagnostics, not `Schema.Unknown` causes.
  No tagged-error payload field may use `Schema.Unknown`. Preserve defects as
  defects, or map only safe diagnostic fields at the true adapter boundary.
- Service-contract scopes reject direct `unknown` parameter annotations and
  direct `Effect.Effect<Success, unknown, Requirements>` error positions.
  Current syntax-only enforcement does not follow aliases to prove that an
  interface is a `Context.Service` contract, infer semantic identity through
  arbitrary schema composition, or prove a decoder binding has one real use.
  Keep those cases under schema/service review until a narrow AST shape is
  demonstrated; do not add a filename loophole or a sidecar lint script.
- One-off `Effect.map`, `Effect.mapError`, `Effect.catchTag`,
  `Effect.catchAll`, `Result`, or `Exit` handling should stay inline at the
  callsite unless it becomes a real reusable boundary policy.

## Optional Values

Optional request, response, frontmatter, SEO, and loader fields should be owned
by schemas. Branch with `Option.match`, `Option.isSome`, or `Option.isNone`
when behavior depends on presence.

Keep internal absence as `Option` or schema-owned optional fields. Avoid
`Option.getOrNull`, raw `null` object properties, and `Schema.NullOr` in
internal service code unless the module is explicitly modeling an external
protocol boundary.

Do not build schema-backed objects with conditional spreads:

```ts
{
  ...(description ? { description } : {})
}
```

Fix the owning schema or construct the optional value through `Option` at the
boundary. If a field should be required, make it required in the schema instead
of repeatedly omitting it at callsites.

## Functional Composition

Use pipe-first composition when sequencing transformations or Effect programs
is clearer left-to-right. Avoid nested wrapper calls such as
`toOutput(transformInput(input))` when the same flow reads better as a pipeline.

Use named reusable operations only when they own a durable policy, cross a
package boundary, or remove meaningful repeated complexity.

Do not extract one-line mapper/adapter helpers named like `map*`, `to*`,
`decode*`, `encode*`, or `normalize*` only to pass them into `Effect.map`,
`Effect.mapError`, Schema encode/decode helpers, or RPC adapter mapping. Inline
the one-off transform or move real encode/decode behavior into the owning schema
or service contract.

## Route And Middleware Boundaries

Canonical route-owned Markdown negotiation must stay redirect-only:
`@packages/aeo` owns schema-backed Accept-only decisions and Markdown
sibling redirect targets, `@packages/effect-start` owns reusable TanStack
Start/Effect middleware adapters, and `apps/web` owns the concrete route
registry plus route-owned `.md` rendering. Do not add Markdown body rendering,
route registries, or app-specific DTO mirrors to reusable packages.

The sole allowed TanStack server-function exception is
`apps/web/src/lib/http/markdown-sibling-redirect.middleware.ts`, where
`createServerOnlyFn` fences the dynamic import of the `.server.ts` handler.
TanStack production import protection rejects a direct `runtime.server` import
through `src/start.ts`, and `site/no-unscoped-tanstack-server-functions`
prevents broader server-function usage.

Specs and implementation tasks that change route/runtime/SEO/AEO behavior must
include production and test call graphs, direct route evidence, and Browser
screenshot evidence for the affected visible route or OG surface.

## Open Graph Platform Adapters

`@packages/og` owns the schema-derived renderer request/result contracts,
`OgRenderer`, `TakumiClient`, the dependency-requiring
`OgRendererTakumiLayer`, and the composed `OgRendererNativeLive`. The native
layer provides `TakumiClientLive` through `Layer.provide`. App OG services
consume `OgRenderer`; they do not import Takumi directly or mirror package
contracts with local DTOs.

The sole generic `takumi-js` render import is
`apps/web/src/lib/deployment/cloudflare/og.layer.ts`. That file is the
Cloudflare platform adapter and owns the bundled Worker-compatible
`WebAssembly.Module`. It implements the canonical `OgRenderer` service, wraps
the Promise API with `Effect.tryPromise`, validates the result with the owning
schema, and maps the complete render/decode program once to `OgRenderError`.
Do not add generic Takumi imports to package, Bun, server, script, route, or
test code. Deep Takumi helper and native imports remain internal to the
package-owned `TakumiClientLive` adapter.

Keep app OG asset, render-data, and output values schema-derived. Service
contracts may name Effect operations over those canonical types, while pure
React component props and inferred visual constants may remain TypeScript-only.
Do not add route-local error mirrors: the HTTP boundary handles canonical post,
asset, schema, and render error tags directly.

## Frontend Route Composition

Routes own their visible layout tree. Compose `PageShell`, `PageHeader`,
`PageSection`, `ProsePage`, `IndexFeed`, `MetadataRow`, and `RouteErrorBlock`
as high in the route file as possible instead of hiding complete page bodies in
route component values named `*Page`. Use route-owned `*Route` component names
when TanStack needs a component function.

Use explicit `gap-*` rhythm in primitives and route layouts. Do not introduce
`space-x-*` or `space-y-*`; those utilities couple spacing to child order and
are harder to audit across route-owned layouts.

Browser-mode route component tests should exercise TanStack Router behavior:
render through `RouterProvider` with `createMemoryHistory`, keep route
components private to their route files, and use route-owned `Link` markup.
When the full generated route tree would import server-only modules, build a
narrow test route tree from the exported route objects and the same UI
providers required by production.

# Code Patterns

This repo uses Effect-native TypeScript for boundary-crossing, fallible,
runtime-owned, schema-owned, or service-owned code. UI-only rendering can stay
plain React, but package code, loaders, runtime setup, RPC, config, command
execution, and content validation should prefer Effect primitives.

The boundary rules in this document are lint-backed through normal
`bun run check`: portable Effect rules live under `effect/*`, Bun runtime rules
under `bun/*`, portable MDX rendering rules under `mdx/*`, and this site's
route, SEO/AEO, TanStack, typography, and design-system policies under
`site/*`.

Use `Data`, `Schema`, `Array`, `Chunk`, `HashSet`, `HashMap`, `Match`,
`Context`, `Layer`, `Config`, `Service`, `Record`, `Option`, `Result`, `Exit`,
Bun/Platform `Command`, and `ManagedRuntime` before adding ad hoc TypeScript
helpers for those concerns.

## Boundary Values

- Define package, RPC, loader, config, command, and content boundary values with
  `Schema`.
- Derive TypeScript types from schemas with `typeof Schema.Type`.
- Reuse canonical schema-derived types, branded identifiers, service tags,
  tagged errors, and constructors from the owning package.
- Do not mirror canonical fields as local primitives such as `id: string`,
  `slug: string`, `title: string`, or post metadata outside their owning schema
  or service projection.
- Decode unknown input once at an explicit package, RPC, loader, config,
  command, HTTP, provider, filesystem, or content ingress with the owning
  Effect Schema. `schemas.ts` declares codecs; it is not a runtime-boundary
  exception.
- Encode only at serialization egresses such as HTTP/RPC responses, loader
  codecs, reports, command output, persisted state, or provider requests.
- Use `Schema.TaggedClass`, `Schema.TaggedError`, `Schema.TaggedStruct`, or
  `Data.TaggedClass` when a variant crosses a boundary. Import
  `Schema.TaggedError` as lower-case `taggedError` when Ultracite's generic
  `throw-new-error` rule would otherwise mistake the Effect constructor for a
  thrown JavaScript error.

## Effects, Layers, And Services

- `service.ts` files own `Context.Service` contracts and canonical request,
  response, and error shapes.
- Production wiring belongs in `live.layer.ts` or an explicit runtime/layer
  module, not in service contract files.
- Package and service code should return `Effect` values and layers. Runtime
  execution belongs in app route loaders, runtime files, server files, scripts,
  or package boundary modules that own a process/runtime lifecycle.
- Expected failures should be tagged schema errors returned through
  `Effect.fail`, `Effect.try`, or `Effect.tryPromise`, not thrown exceptions.
  Raw `try` statements are banned by `effect/no-try-statement`, including
  `try/finally`. Use Effect/Result error handling and scoped finalisation.
- Fallible Promise APIs enter through import-aware, lint-enforced
  `Effect.tryPromise({ try, catch })` boundaries. Bare callback-form
  `Effect.tryPromise` is forbidden because it leaves rejection policy implicit.
- Raw `async`, `await`, and `new Promise` are not allowed in Effect-owned
  service/runtime scopes. External Promise APIs enter through
  `Effect.promise` or `Effect.tryPromise`; keep catch mapping inline and tagged
  at that boundary.
- `process.env` and `process.argv` reads belong in explicit config, runtime,
  main, CLI, layer, adapter, or test boundaries. `console.*`,
  `Effect.runPromise`, `BunRuntime.runMain`, and `ManagedRuntime.make` belong in
  runtime, main, CLI, layer, adapter, or test boundaries. Direct host APIs and
  provider SDKs belong in live layer, runtime, CLI, or adapter modules. Package
  logic returns typed values, tagged errors, Effects, and Layers.
- Do not call throwing `Schema` or `SchemaParser` `*Sync` codecs in production,
  including top-level constants and runtime modules. Use effectful codecs at
  ingress/egress so parse failures remain in the Effect error channel.
  Non-throwing `Result`/`Exit`/`Option` decoders are reserved for synchronous
  consumers such as loader hydration, deterministic fixtures, and tests.
- `decodeTo` and `encodeTo` are schema transformations, not runtime codec
  execution. They do not establish an ingress or egress boundary.
- Tagged errors expose schema-safe diagnostics, not `Schema.Unknown` causes.
  No tagged-error payload field may use `Schema.Unknown`. Preserve defects as
  defects, or map only safe diagnostic fields at the true adapter boundary.
- Service-contract scopes reject direct `unknown` parameter annotations and
  direct `Effect.Effect<Success, unknown, Requirements>` error positions.
  Current syntax-only enforcement does not follow aliases to prove that an
  interface is a `Context.Service` contract, infer semantic identity through
  arbitrary schema composition, or prove a decoder binding has one real use.
  Keep those cases under schema/service review until a narrow AST shape is
  demonstrated; do not add a filename loophole or a sidecar lint script.
- One-off `Effect.map`, `Effect.mapError`, `Effect.catchTag`,
  `Effect.catchAll`, `Result`, or `Exit` handling should stay inline at the
  callsite unless it becomes a real reusable boundary policy.

## Optional Values

Optional request, response, frontmatter, SEO, and loader fields should be owned
by schemas. Branch with `Option.match`, `Option.isSome`, or `Option.isNone`
when behavior depends on presence.

Keep internal absence as `Option` or schema-owned optional fields. Avoid
`Option.getOrNull`, raw `null` object properties, and `Schema.NullOr` in
internal service code unless the module is explicitly modeling an external
protocol boundary.

Do not build schema-backed objects with conditional spreads:

```ts
{
  ...(description ? { description } : {})
}
```

Fix the owning schema or construct the optional value through `Option` at the
boundary. If a field should be required, make it required in the schema instead
of repeatedly omitting it at callsites.

## Functional Composition

Use pipe-first composition when sequencing transformations or Effect programs
is clearer left-to-right. Avoid nested wrapper calls such as
`toOutput(transformInput(input))` when the same flow reads better as a pipeline.

Use named reusable operations only when they own a durable policy, cross a
package boundary, or remove meaningful repeated complexity.

Do not extract one-line mapper/adapter helpers named like `map*`, `to*`,
`decode*`, `encode*`, or `normalize*` only to pass them into `Effect.map`,
`Effect.mapError`, Schema encode/decode helpers, or RPC adapter mapping. Inline
the one-off transform or move real encode/decode behavior into the owning schema
or service contract.

## Route And Middleware Boundaries

Canonical route-owned Markdown negotiation must stay redirect-only:
`@packages/aeo` owns schema-backed Accept-only decisions and Markdown
sibling redirect targets, `@packages/effect-start` owns reusable TanStack
Start/Effect middleware adapters, and `apps/web` owns the concrete route
registry plus route-owned `.md` rendering. Do not add Markdown body rendering,
route registries, or app-specific DTO mirrors to reusable packages.

The sole allowed TanStack server-function exception is
`apps/web/src/lib/http/markdown-sibling-redirect.middleware.ts`, where
`createServerOnlyFn` fences the dynamic import of the `.server.ts` handler.
TanStack production import protection rejects a direct `runtime.server` import
through `src/start.ts`, and `site/no-unscoped-tanstack-server-functions`
prevents broader server-function usage.

Specs and implementation tasks that change route/runtime/SEO/AEO behavior must
include production and test call graphs, direct route evidence, and Browser
screenshot evidence for the affected visible route or OG surface.

## Open Graph Platform Adapters

`@packages/og` owns the schema-derived renderer request/result contracts,
`OgRenderer`, `TakumiClient`, the dependency-requiring
`OgRendererTakumiLayer`, and the composed `OgRendererNativeLive`. The native
layer provides `TakumiClientLive` through `Layer.provide`. App OG services
consume `OgRenderer`; they do not import Takumi directly or mirror package
contracts with local DTOs.

The sole generic `takumi-js` render import is
`apps/web/src/lib/deployment/cloudflare/og.layer.ts`. That file is the
Cloudflare platform adapter and owns the bundled Worker-compatible
`WebAssembly.Module`. It implements the canonical `OgRenderer` service, wraps
the Promise API with `Effect.tryPromise`, validates the result with the owning
schema, and maps the complete render/decode program once to `OgRenderError`.
Do not add generic Takumi imports to package, Bun, server, script, route, or
test code. Deep Takumi helper and native imports remain internal to the
package-owned `TakumiClientLive` adapter.

Keep app OG asset, render-data, and output values schema-derived. Service
contracts may name Effect operations over those canonical types, while pure
React component props and inferred visual constants may remain TypeScript-only.
Do not add route-local error mirrors: the HTTP boundary handles canonical post,
asset, schema, and render error tags directly.

## Frontend Route Composition

Routes own their visible layout tree. Compose `PageShell`, `PageHeader`,
`PageSection`, `ProsePage`, `IndexFeed`, `MetadataRow`, and `RouteErrorBlock`
as high in the route file as possible instead of hiding complete page bodies in
route component values named `*Page`. Use route-owned `*Route` component names
when TanStack needs a component function.

Use explicit `gap-*` rhythm in primitives and route layouts. Do not introduce
`space-x-*` or `space-y-*`; those utilities couple spacing to child order and
are harder to audit across route-owned layouts.

Browser-mode route component tests should exercise TanStack Router behavior:
render through `RouterProvider` with `createMemoryHistory`, keep route
components private to their route files, and use route-owned `Link` markup.
When the full generated route tree would import server-only modules, build a
narrow test route tree from the exported route objects and the same UI
providers required by production.

# Tooling

This repo uses Bun workspaces, Ultracite, Oxlint, Oxfmt, Knip, TypeScript
---

confidence: high
  Current syntax-only enforcement does not follow aliases to prove that an
  interface is a `Context.Service` contract, infer semantic identity through
  arbitrary schema composition, or prove a decoder binding has one real use.
  Keep those cases under schema/service review until a narrow AST shape is
  demonstrated; do not add a filename loophole or a sidecar lint script.
- One-off `Effect.map`, `Effect.mapError`, `Effect.catchTag`,
  `Effect.catchAll`, `Result`, or `Exit` handling should stay inline at the
  callsite unless it becomes a real reusable boundary policy.

## Optional Values

Optional request, response, frontmatter, SEO, and loader fields should be owned
by schemas. Branch with `Option.match`, `Option.isSome`, or `Option.isNone`
when behavior depends on presence.

Keep internal absence as `Option` or schema-owned optional fields. Avoid
`Option.getOrNull`, raw `null` object properties, and `Schema.NullOr` in
internal service code unless the module is explicitly modeling an external
protocol boundary.

Do not build schema-backed objects with conditional spreads:

checks the live pull request, owner, repository, label and exact head before
fetching Preview credentials. It derives the stage as `pr-<number>`, rebuilds

The [Production workflow](../../.github/workflows/alchemy-main.yml) requires

the named Production Environment and runs

---
document_type: operations-policy
lifecycle: current
authority: canonical
owner: site-operations-maintainer

# Delivery authority and credential custody

Tool access is not permission. Every provider operation needs an exact
principal, candidate, operation, resource set, environment, approval, receipt,
rollback identity and readback.

## Current boundaries

| Boundary                              | Principal and admission                                                                       | Credential custody                                         | Required record                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Read-only local checks                | repository worker in the current checkout                                                     | no provider credential                                     | command, candidate, result and limits                                               |
| Pull-request Preview deploy           | trusted same-repository PR, exact accepted head, Preview policy and Environment configuration | Preview Environment `DOPPLER_TOKEN` for `site/stg_preview` | PR, head, stage, apply/Website receipt, Worker identity, routes and telemetry       |
| Exact Preview cleanup                 | trusted default-branch close/label-removal workflow for the same PR                           | same Preview bootstrap token                               | PR, stage, saved-state target, absence readback and limits                          |
| Production deploy                     | Cooper's exact accepted `main` SHA and Production Environment configuration                   | Production Environment `DOPPLER_TOKEN` for `site/prd`      | SHA, apply/Website receipt, Worker/version, twelve dashboards, routes and telemetry |
| Credential or provider administration | separately approved named operator                                                            | provider or Doppler administration boundary                | exact mutation, before/after metadata, revocation and recovery                      |

The repository implementation does not grant authority by itself. An active
task may attach an explicit operation record for its authorised deploy,
state-read and proof scope; that record does not authorise cleanup, unrelated
account work or a merge.

## Doppler contract

The supported configs are:

- `site/stg_preview` for `pr-<number>` Preview;
- `site/prd` for `prod` Production.

Each supplies exactly:

- `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`;
- `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`;
- `AXIOM_TOKEN`.

GitHub stores only the environment-scoped read-only `DOPPLER_TOKEN` that can
fetch the matching config. Provider values must not be copied into repository
files, GitHub variables or secrets, shell arguments, logs, artifacts,
receipts, clipboard reads or chat.

The Preview Axiom credential needs only the provider access required to create
and delete stage-scoped ingest tokens, run the bounded candidate query and
read the exact affected resources. Cleanup also requires dashboard read access
to compare the twelve canonical Site dashboards before and after destroy; it
does not require dashboard create, update or delete access. The Axiom token
API scopes dashboard read to the organisation, so record that metadata-access
limitation in the credential receipt. Production additionally manages the three
shared datasets and twelve dashboards. Any wider unavoidable permission is a
recorded risk, not an implied grant.

## Candidate and operation binding

A Preview operation is bound to one PR number, exact head SHA and derived
`pr-<number>` stage. Production is bound to one exact accepted main SHA and the
literal `prod` stage. Neither command accepts an arbitrary provider namespace.

An optional native plan is diagnostic only. Delivery invokes native deploy once,
writes an apply-completed receipt before state read, and exposes a separate
read-only provider/public verification command. These implementation limits do
not relax any existing approval requirement. Cleanup has its own event and
approval boundary; deploy permission does not automatically permit deletion.

Native `--yes` also permits `Cloudflare.state()` backend bootstrap/upgrade.
Cold state login can also create a temporary edge-preview session to recover
the state auth secret, including for state reads without `--yes`. That is not
a Production deployment, but it is a provider consequence. Neither capability
is separate state-administration or authentication-operation authority. If the exact
operation would exceed its approval, stop. The completed [native delivery
plan](../exec-plans/completed/alchemy-native-delivery.md) records the accepted
task-scoped source/stage/run/operation and native-state authority decisions as
history. A new operation needs its own authority; the completed plan does not
grant account-wide access or a merge.

## Fail closed

Stop before provider access when candidate, source digest, stage,
environment or required named credential is absent or mismatched. Stop during
provider work on permission, quota, entitlement, state ownership or readback
failure. Do not add duplicate expected identity settings to pre-approve a
credential; use the actual Alchemy/provider operation and sanitised result.

An unavailable check remains unavailable. Do not rewrite an old receipt or
promote a local check to hosted, provider or public proof.

## Revocation and recovery

- A leaked or over-broad credential needs separate rotation authority and
  readback that the old credential is unusable.
- A failed Preview may be cleaned only through the exact Preview cleanup path.
- A failed Production release recovers through a new or reverted main
  candidate and the same native deploy/readback checks.
- Removing an obsolete GitHub Environment, Doppler config or live resource is
  a separate external mutation with exact before/after readback.

Historical receipts remain evidence of their own operation only. They do not
keep an obsolete delivery path current.
name: Alchemy Main Delivery

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      commit_sha:
        description: Exact commit SHA accepted by the caller quality job
        required: true
        type: string
      quality_sha:
        description: Exact commit SHA emitted by the caller quality job
        required: true
        type: string
      runner_label:
        description: Trusted runner label; defaults to GitHub-hosted Ubuntu
        required: false
        default: ubuntu-latest
        type: string
    secrets:
      DOPPLER_TOKEN:
        description: Named slot supplied by the Production Environment credential mapping
        required: false

permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: read

env:
  ALCHEMY_PROFILE: site-ci-env-v1

concurrency:
  group: site-alchemy-main
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  production_deploy:
    name: Deploy Production Alchemy graph
    if: >-
      github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
      inputs.commit_sha == github.sha &&
      inputs.quality_sha == inputs.commit_sha
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner_label }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    environment: production
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Check out reviewed commit
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7; Site infrastructure/security maintainer owns pin updates
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          ref: ${{ inputs.commit_sha }}
      - name: Set up Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2; Site infrastructure/security maintainer owns pin updates
        with:
          bun-version-file: ".bun-version"
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Fetch Production secrets from Doppler
        id: doppler
        uses: dopplerhq/secrets-fetch-action@451892f16195f9ac360e1a5bcbf0b5fd0e957534 # v2.0.0; Site infrastructure/security maintainer owns pin updates
        with:
          doppler-token: ${{ secrets.DOPPLER_TOKEN }}
      - name: Build web package dependencies
        run: bun turbo run build --filter=web^...
      - name: Deploy Production with Alchemy
        id: production-deploy
        run: bun alchemy deploy --stage prod --yes
        env:
          ALCHEMY_PHASE: deploy
          AXIOM_TOKEN: ${{ steps.doppler.outputs.AXIOM_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ steps.doppler.outputs.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ steps.doppler.outputs.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          GITHUB_SHA: ${{ inputs.commit_sha }}

# Deployment architecture

Alchemy owns deployment of Site's Cloudflare and Axiom resources. The GitHub
quality workflow checks out and tests one exact commit, then passes that SHA

## Current boundaries

| Boundary                              | Principal and admission                                                                       | Credential custody                                         | Required record                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Read-only local checks                | repository worker in the current checkout                                                     | no provider credential                                     | command, candidate, result and limits                                               |
| Pull-request Preview deploy           | trusted same-repository PR, exact accepted head, Preview policy and Environment configuration | Preview Environment `DOPPLER_TOKEN` for `site/stg_preview` | PR, head, stage, apply/Website receipt, Worker identity, routes and telemetry       |
| Exact Preview cleanup                 | trusted default-branch close/label-removal workflow for the same PR                           | same Preview bootstrap token                               | PR, stage, saved-state target, absence readback and limits                          |
| Production deploy                     | Cooper's exact accepted `main` SHA and Production Environment configuration                   | Production Environment `DOPPLER_TOKEN` for `site/prd`      | SHA, apply/Website receipt, Worker/version, twelve dashboards, routes and telemetry |
| Credential or provider administration | separately approved named operator                                                            | provider or Doppler administration boundary                | exact mutation, before/after metadata, revocation and recovery                      |

The repository implementation does not grant authority by itself. An active
task may attach an explicit operation record for its authorised deploy,
state-read and proof scope; that record does not authorise cleanup, unrelated
account work or a merge.

## Doppler contract

The supported configs are:

- `site/stg_preview` for `pr-<number>` Preview;
- `site/prd` for `prod` Production.

Each supplies exactly:

- `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`;
- `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`;
- `AXIOM_TOKEN`.

GitHub stores only the environment-scoped read-only `DOPPLER_TOKEN` that can
fetch the matching config. Provider values must not be copied into repository
files, GitHub variables or secrets, shell arguments, logs, artifacts,
receipts, clipboard reads or chat.

The Preview Axiom credential needs only the provider access required to create
and delete stage-scoped ingest tokens, run the bounded candidate query and
read the exact affected resources. Cleanup also requires dashboard read access
to compare the twelve canonical Site dashboards before and after destroy; it
does not require dashboard create, update or delete access. The Axiom token
API scopes dashboard read to the organisation, so record that metadata-access
limitation in the credential receipt. Production additionally manages the three
shared datasets and twelve dashboards. Any wider unavoidable permission is a
recorded risk, not an implied grant.

## Candidate and operation binding

A Preview operation is bound to one PR number, exact head SHA and derived
`pr-<number>` stage. Production is bound to one exact accepted main SHA and the
literal `prod` stage. Neither command accepts an arbitrary provider namespace.

An optional native plan is diagnostic only. Delivery invokes native deploy once,
writes an apply-completed receipt before state read, and exposes a separate
read-only provider/public verification command. These implementation limits do
not relax any existing approval requirement. Cleanup has its own event and
approval boundary; deploy permission does not automatically permit deletion.

Native `--yes` also permits `Cloudflare.state()` backend bootstrap/upgrade.
Cold state login can also create a temporary edge-preview session to recover
the state auth secret, including for state reads without `--yes`. That is not
a Production deployment, but it is a provider consequence. Neither capability
is separate state-administration or authentication-operation authority. If the exact
operation would exceed its approval, stop. The completed [native delivery
plan](../exec-plans/completed/alchemy-native-delivery.md) records the accepted
task-scoped source/stage/run/operation and native-state authority decisions as
history. A new operation needs its own authority; the completed plan does not
grant account-wide access or a merge.

## Fail closed

Stop before provider access when candidate, source digest, stage,
environment or required named credential is absent or mismatched. Stop during
provider work on permission, quota, entitlement, state ownership or readback
failure. Do not add duplicate expected identity settings to pre-approve a
credential; use the actual Alchemy/provider operation and sanitised result.

An unavailable check remains unavailable. Do not rewrite an old receipt or
promote a local check to hosted, provider or public proof.

## Revocation and recovery

- A leaked or over-broad credential needs separate rotation authority and
  readback that the old credential is unusable.
- A failed Preview may be cleaned only through the exact Preview cleanup path.
- A failed Production release recovers through a new or reverted main
  candidate and the same native deploy/readback checks.
- Removing an obsolete GitHub Environment, Doppler config or live resource is
  a separate external mutation with exact before/after readback.

Historical receipts remain evidence of their own operation only. They do not
keep an obsolete delivery path current.
name: Alchemy Main Delivery

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      commit_sha:
        description: Exact commit SHA accepted by the caller quality job
        required: true
        type: string
      quality_sha:
        description: Exact commit SHA emitted by the caller quality job
        required: true
        type: string
      runner_label:
        description: Trusted runner label; defaults to GitHub-hosted Ubuntu
        required: false
        default: ubuntu-latest
        type: string
    secrets:
      DOPPLER_TOKEN:
        description: Named slot supplied by the Production Environment credential mapping
        required: false

permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: read

env:
  ALCHEMY_PROFILE: site-ci-env-v1

concurrency:
  group: site-alchemy-main
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  production_deploy:
    name: Deploy Production Alchemy graph
    if: >-
      github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
      inputs.commit_sha == github.sha &&
      inputs.quality_sha == inputs.commit_sha
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner_label }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    environment: production
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Check out reviewed commit
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7; Site infrastructure/security maintainer owns pin updates
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          ref: ${{ inputs.commit_sha }}
      - name: Set up Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2; Site infrastructure/security maintainer owns pin updates
        with:
          bun-version-file: ".bun-version"
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Fetch Production secrets from Doppler
        id: doppler
        uses: dopplerhq/secrets-fetch-action@451892f16195f9ac360e1a5bcbf0b5fd0e957534 # v2.0.0; Site infrastructure/security maintainer owns pin updates
        with:
          doppler-token: ${{ secrets.DOPPLER_TOKEN }}
      - name: Build web package dependencies
        run: bun turbo run build --filter=web^...
      - name: Deploy Production with Alchemy
        id: production-deploy
        run: bun alchemy deploy --stage prod --yes
        env:
          ALCHEMY_PHASE: deploy
          AXIOM_TOKEN: ${{ steps.doppler.outputs.AXIOM_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ steps.doppler.outputs.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ steps.doppler.outputs.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          GITHUB_SHA: ${{ inputs.commit_sha }}

## Preview

The [Preview workflow](../../.github/workflows/cloudflare-branch-preview.yml)
checks the live pull request, owner, repository, label and exact head before
fetching Preview credentials. It derives the stage as `pr-<number>`, rebuilds
the accepted checkout, checks generated assets and runs
`bun alchemy deploy --stage "pr-<number>" --yes`.

The [cleanup workflow](../../.github/workflows/cloudflare-branch-preview-cleanup.yml)
uses trusted default-branch code, checks the current pull request again, and
runs `bun alchemy destroy alchemy.destroy.ts --stage "pr-<number>" --yes`.
Shared Production datasets and dashboards are outside that stage.

## Production

The [Production workflow](../../.github/workflows/alchemy-main.yml) requires
`main`, the current GitHub SHA and the same SHA accepted by quality. It uses
the named Production Environment and runs
`bun alchemy deploy --stage prod --yes`.

# Deployment architecture

Alchemy owns deployment of Site's Cloudflare and Axiom resources. The GitHub
quality workflow checks out and tests one exact commit, then passes that SHA
to the delivery workflow. Delivery calls native Alchemy once.

## Preview

The [Preview workflow](../../.github/workflows/cloudflare-branch-preview.yml)
checks the live pull request, owner, repository, label and exact head before
fetching Preview credentials. It derives the stage as `pr-<number>`, rebuilds
the accepted checkout, checks generated assets and runs
`bun alchemy deploy --stage "pr-<number>" --yes`.

The [cleanup workflow](../../.github/workflows/cloudflare-branch-preview-cleanup.yml)
uses trusted default-branch code, checks the current pull request again, and
runs `bun alchemy destroy alchemy.destroy.ts --stage "pr-<number>" --yes`.
Shared Production datasets and dashboards are outside that stage.

## Production

The [Production workflow](../../.github/workflows/alchemy-main.yml) requires
`main`, the current GitHub SHA and the same SHA accepted by quality. It uses
the named Production Environment and runs
`bun alchemy deploy --stage prod --yes`.

Production deployment is supported through that workflow. There is no local
Production deploy wrapper. The root `production:plan` command remains an
optional native Alchemy diagnostic.

## Credentials and runtime telemetry

Doppler supplies `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and
`AXIOM_TOKEN` to the native Alchemy step through the matching GitHub
Environment. The workflow selects `ALCHEMY_PROFILE=site-ci-env-v1`; GitHub
provides non-interactive CI mode. Credentials are not printed or retained.

Alchemy still declares datasets, dashboards, tokens, destinations and metrics
secrets. The application still records ordinary request metrics, and Cloudflare
exports logs and traces. There are no special proof-marker requests or custom
post-deploy Cloudflare, public-route, dashboard or Axiom verification commands.

## Results and recovery

The native command's exit status determines delivery success or failure. Its
output remains in the ordinary workflow log. A successful command reports
Alchemy completion; it does not establish ongoing public availability or
telemetry ingestion.

Release tags and Changesets remain release metadata. Lighthouse, application
tests and browser checks remain part of local quality. Their results do not
claim a Production deployment.

Recover through a new or reverted exact commit and the same quality and Alchemy
workflow. Use [the incident runbook](../runbooks/cloudflare/incident-and-rollback.md)
for an incident. Provider repair, credential changes and resource teardown
remain separate operations. The native state entrypoint
[`alchemy.state.run.ts`](../../alchemy.state.run.ts) remains available for
authorised investigation.

The [Preview](../runbooks/cloudflare/preview-lifecycle.md) and
[Production](../runbooks/cloudflare/production-deploy.md) runbooks own the
operating steps.

# Delivery authority and credential custody

Tool access is not permission. Every provider operation needs an exact
principal, candidate, operation, resource set, environment, approval, receipt,
rollback identity and readback.

## Current boundaries

| Boundary                              | Principal and admission                                                                       | Credential custody                                         | Required record                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Read-only local checks                | repository worker in the current checkout                                                     | no provider credential                                     | command, candidate, result and limits                                               |
| Pull-request Preview deploy           | trusted same-repository PR, exact accepted head, Preview policy and Environment configuration | Preview Environment `DOPPLER_TOKEN` for `site/stg_preview` | PR, head, stage, apply/Website receipt, Worker identity, routes and telemetry       |
| Exact Preview cleanup                 | trusted default-branch close/label-removal workflow for the same PR                           | same Preview bootstrap token                               | PR, stage, saved-state target, absence readback and limits                          |
| Production deploy                     | Cooper's exact accepted `main` SHA and Production Environment configuration                   | Production Environment `DOPPLER_TOKEN` for `site/prd`      | SHA, apply/Website receipt, Worker/version, twelve dashboards, routes and telemetry |
| Credential or provider administration | separately approved named operator                                                            | provider or Doppler administration boundary                | exact mutation, before/after metadata, revocation and recovery                      |

The repository implementation does not grant authority by itself. An active
task may attach an explicit operation record for its authorised deploy,
state-read and proof scope; that record does not authorise cleanup, unrelated
account work or a merge.

## Doppler contract

The supported configs are:

- `site/stg_preview` for `pr-<number>` Preview;
- `site/prd` for `prod` Production.

Each supplies exactly:

- `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`;
- `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`;
- `AXIOM_TOKEN`.

GitHub stores only the environment-scoped read-only `DOPPLER_TOKEN` that can
fetch the matching config. Provider values must not be copied into repository
files, GitHub variables or secrets, shell arguments, logs, artifacts,
receipts, clipboard reads or chat.

The Preview Axiom credential needs only the provider access required to create
and delete stage-scoped ingest tokens, run the bounded candidate query and
read the exact affected resources. Cleanup also requires dashboard read access
to compare the twelve canonical Site dashboards before and after destroy; it
does not require dashboard create, update or delete access. The Axiom token
API scopes dashboard read to the organisation, so record that metadata-access
limitation in the credential receipt. Production additionally manages the three
shared datasets and twelve dashboards. Any wider unavoidable permission is a
recorded risk, not an implied grant.

## Candidate and operation binding

A Preview operation is bound to one PR number, exact head SHA and derived
`pr-<number>` stage. Production is bound to one exact accepted main SHA and the
literal `prod` stage. Neither command accepts an arbitrary provider namespace.

An optional native plan is diagnostic only. Delivery invokes native deploy once,
writes an apply-completed receipt before state read, and exposes a separate
read-only provider/public verification command. These implementation limits do
not relax any existing approval requirement. Cleanup has its own event and
approval boundary; deploy permission does not automatically permit deletion.

Native `--yes` also permits `Cloudflare.state()` backend bootstrap/upgrade.
Cold state login can also create a temporary edge-preview session to recover
the state auth secret, including for state reads without `--yes`. That is not
a Production deployment, but it is a provider consequence. Neither capability
is separate state-administration or authentication-operation authority. If the exact
operation would exceed its approval, stop. The completed [native delivery
plan](../exec-plans/completed/alchemy-native-delivery.md) records the accepted
task-scoped source/stage/run/operation and native-state authority decisions as
history. A new operation needs its own authority; the completed plan does not
grant account-wide access or a merge.

## Fail closed

Stop before provider access when candidate, source digest, stage,
environment or required named credential is absent or mismatched. Stop during
provider work on permission, quota, entitlement, state ownership or readback
failure. Do not add duplicate expected identity settings to pre-approve a
credential; use the actual Alchemy/provider operation and sanitised result.

An unavailable check remains unavailable. Do not rewrite an old receipt or
promote a local check to hosted, provider or public proof.

## Revocation and recovery

- A leaked or over-broad credential needs separate rotation authority and
  readback that the old credential is unusable.
- A failed Preview may be cleaned only through the exact Preview cleanup path.
- A failed Production release recovers through a new or reverted main
  candidate and the same native deploy/readback checks.
- Removing an obsolete GitHub Environment, Doppler config or live resource is
  a separate external mutation with exact before/after readback.

Historical receipts remain evidence of their own operation only. They do not
keep an obsolete delivery path current.
name: Alchemy Main Delivery

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      commit_sha:
        description: Exact commit SHA accepted by the caller quality job
        required: true
        type: string
      quality_sha:
        description: Exact commit SHA emitted by the caller quality job
        required: true
        type: string
      runner_label:
        description: Trusted runner label; defaults to GitHub-hosted Ubuntu
        required: false
        default: ubuntu-latest
        type: string
    secrets:
      DOPPLER_TOKEN:
        description: Named slot supplied by the Production Environment credential mapping
        required: false

permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: read

env:
  ALCHEMY_PROFILE: site-ci-env-v1

concurrency:
  group: site-alchemy-main
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  production_deploy:
    name: Deploy Production Alchemy graph
    if: >-
      github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
      inputs.commit_sha == github.sha &&
      inputs.quality_sha == inputs.commit_sha
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner_label }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    environment: production
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read

# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images, videos, and audio using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When an app or connector generates or edits media, prefer native media already displayed inline or a local output file already returned by the tool. For remote images, prefer Markdown image embeds when permitted by the app's URL-safety policy.
- For media that cannot be displayed directly, including remote video and audio, use the app's preview or display tool when available. Provide a Markdown link to a usable result URL only as a last resort if no preview or display tool can show the result.
- Do not download remote media to work around display restrictions.
- When sending or referencing a local image, video, or audio file, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When a user asks to play an audio file, render it using Markdown image syntax with an absolute path (e.g., ![audio](/absolute/path.mp3)).
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Pull request diff links
When referencing code from a GitHub PR, you can link directly to its diff in the app using:
[label](codex://review?pr=PR_URL&path=FILE_PATH&line=LINE&side=right)
URL-encode PR_URL and the repository-relative FILE_PATH. Use a verified one-based LINE from the current PR diff. Use side=left for the original code or side=right for the updated code. Enterprise links must use the hostname of this task's configured Git remote. Use ordinary file links for workspace code.

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, use the MCP server's `load_workspace_dependencies` tool (`mcp__codex_app__load_workspace_dependencies`) to find the bundled runtime and libraries.

### Automations
- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.
- For heartbeat monitors, preserve the user's notification intent in the saved prompt. Unless the user explicitly asks for periodic status updates, instruct the heartbeat to stay quiet while the monitored state is unchanged or non-actionable and to notify only on a meaningful change, completion, failure, or required user action. Do not add instructions such as "leave a brief status update" on every run.
- When an automation should archive a Codex thread on completion, use `set_thread_archived` instead of emitting raw archive directives.

### Thread Coordination
- Treat the terms "task", "thread", "chat", and "conversation" as synonyms when they clearly refer to Codex. Tool names use the term "thread" and Codex uses "task" in the UI. When providing user-facing responses, use "task".
- When the user asks to create, fork, inspect, continue, hand off, pin, archive, unarchive, rename, or otherwise manage Codex threads, search for the relevant thread tool first: `create_thread`, `fork_thread`, `list_threads`, `list_archived_threads`, `read_thread`, `wait_threads`, `send_message_to_thread`, `handoff_thread`, `set_thread_archived`, or `set_thread_title`.
- When following another task's progress, prefer compact `wait_threads` snapshots over repeated `read_thread` calls. Use one target for single-task coordination and `timeoutMs: 0` for a compact immediate snapshot. `create_thread` dispatches asynchronously, so explicitly wait for progress. Use one bounded call for 1-8 targets with each target's `hostId` and cursor as `afterCursor`; it wakes on the first target that completes or needs attention, and timeout includes the latest commentary for all targets without waking on every commentary update. An up-to-date cursor suppresses already-delivered final text. Separate waits from one task may run serially. Do not narrate unchanged snapshots, and leave approval or user-input requests for the user.
- Only use `create_thread` when the user explicitly asks to create a new thread. Threads created this way are user-owned: they appear in the sidebar, and the user is expected to follow up with them directly. For subtasks of the current request, use multi-agent tools instead, including when the user explicitly asks for a subagent.
- After a successful `create_thread` call, emit `::created-thread{threadId="..."}` for a created thread or `::created-thread{clientThreadId="..."}` for queued worktree setup on its own line in your final response.

### Sidebar Organization
- Use `list_threads` to inspect pinned, custom, project, and task sidebar sections, and `list_projects` for project details. Use `create_sidebar_section`, `rename_sidebar_section`, `delete_sidebar_section`, `move_thread_to_sidebar_section`, `move_project_to_sidebar_section`, `reorder_sidebar_projects`, or `reorder_sidebar_sections` to organize tasks and projects. Moving an item into the pinned section pins it.

### Inline Code Comments
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive when you need to attach feedback directly to specific code lines.
- Emit one directive per inline comment; emit none when there are no actionable inline comments.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3).
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2}

### Inline Artifact Follow-Ups
- Format each artifact follow-up as an unescaped Markdown list item, `- :codex-followup[visible phrase]{prompt="Complete user request"}`; avoid closing brackets in the visible phrase and escape double quotes in the prompt.

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.

4. If above are not clear and you need exact commands, error text, or precise evidence, search over `rollout_path` for more evidence.

During execution: if you hit repeated errors, confusing behavior, or suspect

How to decide whether to verify memory:

- Consider both risk of drift and verification effort.
- If a fact is likely to drift and is cheap to verify, verify it before
  answering.
- If a fact is likely to drift but verification is expensive, slow, or
  disruptive, it is acceptable to answer from memory in an interactive turn,

  consider offering to refresh it live.
- If a fact is lower-drift and expensive to verify, it is usually fine to

When answering from memory without current verification:

- If you rely on memory for a fact that you did not verify in the current turn,

- If that fact is plausibly drift-prone or comes from an older note, older
  snapshot, or prior run summary, say that it may be stale or outdated.
- If live verification was skipped and a refresh would be useful in the
  interactive context, consider offering to verify or refresh it live.
- Do not present unverified memory-derived facts as confirmed-current.
- Prefer a short refresh offer for interactive questions, especially about prior

Memory citation requirements:

- If ANY relevant memory files were used: append exactly one
`<oai-mem-citation>` block as the VERY LAST content of the final reply.

MEMORY.md:234-236|note=[responsesapi citation extraction code pointer]
rollout_summaries/2026-02-17T21-23-02-LN3m-example.md:10-12|note=[weekly report format]

019c7714-3b77-74d1-9866-e1f484aae2ab
</rollout_ids>
</oai-mem-citation>
```
- `citation_entries` is for rendering:
  - one citation entry per line
  - format: `<file>:<line_start>-<line_end>|note=[<how memory was used>]`
  - use file paths relative to the memory base path (for example, `MEMORY.md`,
    `rollout_summaries/...`, `skills/...`)
  - only cite files actually used under the memory base path (do not cite
    workspace files as memory citations)
  - if you used `MEMORY.md` and then a rollout summary/skill file, cite both
  - list entries in order of importance (most important first)
  - `note` should be short, single-line, and use simple characters only (avoid

lifecycle: current
authority: canonical
owner: site-delivery-maintainer

# Cloudflare Production delivery

Production deploys through the named GitHub Production Environment after
quality accepts the exact `main` commit. This runbook does not authorise a
deployment.

## Preconditions

- The current `main` SHA matches the exact SHA accepted by quality.
- The named Production Environment supplies its required approval.
- Doppler `site/prd` supplies masked `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`,
  `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `AXIOM_TOKEN`.
- Alchemy's `site-ci-env-v1` profile uses environment credentials.

The workflow checks out the accepted SHA, installs the locked dependencies,
builds the web dependencies and calls native Alchemy once:

```sh
bun alchemy deploy --stage prod --yes
```

There is no local Production deploy adapter and no custom post-deploy
verification. The workflow uses Alchemy's exit status and ordinary logs.
The optional root `production:plan` command invokes native Alchemy plan for
diagnostics.

## Resource ownership

The Production graph owns the Website, retained adopted zone and security
settings, three shared Axiom datasets, Production tokens and destinations,
metrics secret and twelve dashboards. Preview owns only its disposable stage
resources. Review destructive or unexpected native plan changes before apply.

## Failure and recovery

Commit mismatch stops the workflow before credentials. A failed native deploy
fails the job. For permission, quota or partial-write failures, inspect the
Alchemy result and affected resource before retrying.

Use `alchemy.state.run.ts` for an authorised native state investigation.
State commands must not use the resource-declaring `alchemy.run.ts` entrypoint.

Recover through a new or reverted `main` commit and the same quality and
Alchemy workflow. Direct provider repair, resource deletion, credential changes
and GitHub Environment changes remain separately approved operations.
See [incident and rollback](incident-and-rollback.md).

A completed Alchemy command is deployment completion, not a claim about ongoing
public availability, dashboard data or telemetry ingestion. Historical proof
reports remain records of their original runs.

## TLS 1.3 and DNSSEC

Before applying the three zone-security declarations, use the existing
Production token from Doppler `site/prd` to read both TLS settings and DNSSEC.
It needs `Zone Settings Write` and the DNSSEC endpoint's accepted `DNS Write`
permission, scoped to the existing zone. A 403 is a permission failure, not
proof that DNSSEC is disabled. Stop before apply if either boundary cannot be
read; do not run a partial security rollout or silently broaden a credential.

Review the plan for `CooperCorbettTls13` (`tls_1_3=on`),
`CooperCorbettMinimumTlsVersion` (`min_tls_version=1.3`) and
`CooperCorbettDnssec` (`status=active`). The two TLS settings affect all
Cloudflare-proxied hostnames in the zone, including unrelated subdomains.
Inspect those hostnames for TLS 1.3 support before release. Older clients that
only support TLS 1.2 will be refused after the minimum changes.

After the normal release, independently read all three settings. Require TLS
1.3 connections to succeed and TLS 1.2 connections to fail at the public apex
and `www`; also check the affected proxied subdomains. DNSSEC is complete only
when Cloudflare reports `active`, the parent publishes the matching DS record
and a validating public resolver returns authenticated answers. Cloudflare
Registrar publishes DS automatically for this registration by periodically
checking CDS/CDNSKEY records. Its [documented first-activation delay](https://developers.cloudflare.com/registrar/get-started/enable-dnssec/)
is one to two days; do not create a DS record inside the child zone. Alchemy accepts `pending`, which is not full
DNSSEC proof. Retain a sanitised dated receipt and a subsequent unchanged plan.

The declarations retain their provider settings on removal. A code rollback
or Website rollback therefore does not turn DNSSEC off or lower TLS. Recovery
requires an explicit reviewed setting change through Alchemy. If DNSSEC must
be disabled, remove the parent DS through the registrar and verify its removal
before stopping zone signing; do not use a generic stack destroy as rollback.
