# Cloudflare Production delivery

Production deploys through the named GitHub Production Environment after
quality accepts the exact `main` commit. This runbook does not authorise a
deployment.

## Preconditions

- The current `main` SHA matches the exact SHA accepted by quality.
- The named Production Environment supplies its required approval.
- Doppler `site/prd` supplies masked `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`,
  `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `AXIOM_TOKEN`.
- Alchemy's `site-ci-env-v1` profile uses environment credentials.

The workflow checks out the accepted SHA, installs the locked dependencies,
builds the web dependencies and calls native Alchemy once:

```sh
bun alchemy deploy --stage prod --yes
```

There is no local Production deploy adapter and no custom post-deploy
verification. The workflow uses Alchemy's exit status and ordinary logs.
The optional root `production:plan` command invokes native Alchemy plan for
diagnostics.

## Resource ownership

The Production graph owns the Website, retained adopted zone and security
settings, three shared Axiom datasets, Production tokens and destinations,
metrics secret and twelve dashboards. Preview owns only its disposable stage
resources. Review destructive or unexpected native plan changes before apply.

## Failure and recovery

Commit mismatch stops the workflow before credentials. A failed native deploy
fails the job. For permission, quota or partial-write failures, inspect the
Alchemy result and affected resource before retrying.

Use `alchemy.state.run.ts` for an authorised native state investigation.
State commands must not use the resource-declaring `alchemy.run.ts` entrypoint.

Recover through a new or reverted `main` commit and the same quality and
Alchemy workflow. Direct provider repair, resource deletion, credential changes
and GitHub Environment changes remain separately approved operations.
See [incident and rollback](incident-and-rollback.md).

A completed Alchemy command is deployment completion, not a claim about ongoing
public availability, dashboard data or telemetry ingestion. Historical proof
reports remain records of their original runs.

## TLS 1.3 and DNSSEC

Before applying the three zone-security declarations, use the existing
Production token from Doppler `site/prd` to read both TLS settings and DNSSEC.
It needs `Zone Settings Write` and the DNSSEC endpoint's accepted `DNS Write`
permission, scoped to the existing zone. A 403 is a permission failure, not
proof that DNSSEC is disabled. Stop before apply if either boundary cannot be
read; do not run a partial security rollout or silently broaden a credential.

Review the plan for `CooperCorbettTls13` (`tls_1_3=on`),
`CooperCorbettMinimumTlsVersion` (`min_tls_version=1.3`) and
`CooperCorbettDnssec` (`status=active`). The two TLS settings affect all
Cloudflare-proxied hostnames in the zone, including unrelated subdomains.
Inspect those hostnames for TLS 1.3 support before release. Older clients that
only support TLS 1.2 will be refused after the minimum changes.

After the normal release, independently read all three settings. Require TLS
1.3 connections to succeed and TLS 1.2 connections to fail at the public apex
and `www`; also check the affected proxied subdomains. DNSSEC is complete only
when Cloudflare reports `active`, the parent publishes the matching DS record
and a validating public resolver returns authenticated answers. Cloudflare
Registrar publishes DS automatically for this registration by periodically
checking CDS/CDNSKEY records. Its [documented first-activation delay](https://developers.cloudflare.com/registrar/get-started/enable-dnssec/)
is one to two days; do not create a DS record inside the child zone. Alchemy accepts `pending`, which is not full
DNSSEC proof. Retain a sanitised dated receipt and a subsequent unchanged plan.

The declarations retain their provider settings on removal. A code rollback
or Website rollback therefore does not turn DNSSEC off or lower TLS. Recovery
requires an explicit reviewed setting change through Alchemy. If DNSSEC must
be disabled, remove the parent DS through the registrar and verify its removal
before stopping zone signing; do not use a generic stack destroy as rollback.

name: Release

on:
  workflow_call:

concurrency:
  group: site-release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  release:
    name: Release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7; Site infrastructure/security maintainer owns pin updates
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Set up Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2; Site infrastructure/security maintainer owns pin updates
        with:
          bun-version-file: ".bun-version"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Create Release Pull Request
        id: changesets
        uses: changesets/action@a45c4d594aa4e2c509dc14a9f2b3b67ba3780d0d # v1.9.0; Site infrastructure/security maintainer owns pin updates
        with:
          version: bun run changeset:version
          commit: "chore: version packages"
          title: "chore: version packages"
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

      - name: Tag the exact released commit
        if: steps.changesets.outputs.hasChangesets == 'false'
        run: bun --filter @packages/scripts release:tags
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

name: Alchemy Main Delivery

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      commit_sha:
        description: Exact commit SHA accepted by the caller quality job
        required: true
        type: string
      quality_sha:
        description: Exact commit SHA emitted by the caller quality job
        required: true
        type: string
      runner_label:
        description: Trusted runner label; defaults to GitHub-hosted Ubuntu
        required: false
        default: ubuntu-latest
        type: string
    secrets:
      DOPPLER_TOKEN:
        description: Named slot supplied by the Production Environment credential mapping
        required: false

permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: read

env:
  ALCHEMY_PROFILE: site-ci-env-v1

concurrency:
  group: site-alchemy-main
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  production_deploy:
    name: Deploy Production Alchemy graph
    if: >-
      github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
      inputs.commit_sha == github.sha &&
      inputs.quality_sha == inputs.commit_sha
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner_label }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    environment: production
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Check out reviewed commit
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7; Site infrastructure/security maintainer owns pin updates
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          ref: ${{ inputs.commit_sha }}
      - name: Set up Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2; Site infrastructure/security maintainer owns pin updates
        with:
          bun-version-file: ".bun-version"
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Fetch Production secrets from Doppler
        id: doppler
        uses: dopplerhq/secrets-fetch-action@451892f16195f9ac360e1a5bcbf0b5fd0e957534 # v2.0.0; Site infrastructure/security maintainer owns pin updates
        with:
          doppler-token: ${{ secrets.DOPPLER_TOKEN }}
      - name: Build web package dependencies
        run: bun turbo run build --filter=web^...
      - name: Deploy Production with Alchemy
        id: production-deploy
        run: bun alchemy deploy --stage prod --yes
        env:
          ALCHEMY_PHASE: deploy
          AXIOM_TOKEN: ${{ steps.doppler.outputs.AXIOM_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ steps.doppler.outputs.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ steps.doppler.outputs.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          GITHUB_SHA: ${{ inputs.commit_sha }}

name: Alchemy Main Delivery

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      commit_sha:
        description: Exact commit SHA accepted by the caller quality job
        required: true
        type: string
      quality_sha:
        description: Exact commit SHA emitted by the caller quality job
        required: true
        type: string
      runner_label:
        description: Trusted runner label; defaults to GitHub-hosted Ubuntu
        required: false
        default: ubuntu-latest
        type: string
    secrets:
      DOPPLER_TOKEN:
        description: Named slot supplied by the Production Environment credential mapping
        required: false

permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: read

env:
  ALCHEMY_PROFILE: site-ci-env-v1

concurrency:
  group: site-alchemy-main
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  production_deploy:
    name: Deploy Production Alchemy graph
    if: >-
      github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
      inputs.commit_sha == github.sha &&
      inputs.quality_sha == inputs.commit_sha
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner_label }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    environment: production
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Check out reviewed commit
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7; Site infrastructure/security maintainer owns pin updates
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          ref: ${{ inputs.commit_sha }}
      - name: Set up Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2; Site infrastructure/security maintainer owns pin updates
        with:
          bun-version-file: ".bun-version"
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Fetch Production secrets from Doppler
        id: doppler
        uses: dopplerhq/secrets-fetch-action@451892f16195f9ac360e1a5bcbf0b5fd0e957534 # v2.0.0; Site infrastructure/security maintainer owns pin updates
        with:
          doppler-token: ${{ secrets.DOPPLER_TOKEN }}
      - name: Build web package dependencies
        run: bun turbo run build --filter=web^...
      - name: Deploy Production with Alchemy
        id: production-deploy
        run: bun alchemy deploy --stage prod --yes
        env:
          ALCHEMY_PHASE: deploy
          AXIOM_TOKEN: ${{ steps.doppler.outputs.AXIOM_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ steps.doppler.outputs.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ steps.doppler.outputs.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          GITHUB_SHA: ${{ inputs.commit_sha }}

# Site infrastructure runbooks

These runbooks own repeatable Site Cloudflare and Alchemy operations. They are
procedures, not proof that an external setting or provider operation exists.
Start with the named runbook, confirm the accepted task and exact target, and
stop when its repository or external prerequisites are absent. Repository
configuration describes desired state; current Alchemy, Cloudflare, Axiom, and
DNS state require separate, dated readback.

| Operation                                   | Owner                                                            | Accepted policy outcome                                                        | Current stop boundary                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Inventory and mutation preflight            | [inventory-and-preflight](cloudflare/inventory-and-preflight.md) | Redacted Executor Personal readback, discrepancy receipt, or inconclusive stop | Reader/query unavailable, target mismatch, or Alchemy/provider views disagree     |
| Preview lifecycle and orphan reconciliation | [preview-lifecycle](cloudflare/preview-lifecycle.md)             | Exact trusted PR head, one native `pr-<number>` deploy and exact-stage cleanup | Missing Preview admission, Doppler mapping, exact commit or cleanup authority     |
| Production delivery                         | [production-deploy](cloudflare/production-deploy.md)             | Exact accepted main SHA, one native `prod` deploy and Alchemy-owned resources  | Missing Production approval, exact commit or recovery identity                    |
| Credentials and remote state                | [credentials-and-state](cloudflare/credentials-and-state.md)     | Least-privilege, target-specific custody with fail-closed readback             | Issuer/custodian contract, revocation path, or exact external task is absent      |
| Incident recovery and rollback              | [incident-and-rollback](cloudflare/incident-and-rollback.md)     | Reverted main commit; Axiom-first investigation; DNS report-only               | Direct rollback, DNS mutation, or destructive observability action                |
| Axiom observability operations              | [site-axiom-observability](site-axiom-observability.md)          | Stage-isolated resource ownership and ordinary telemetry                       | Missing exact task authority, credential custody, provider readback, or ingestion |

## Authority and recovery matrix

| Boundary               | Source of truth                                          | Required approval/receipt                                                                                           | Recovery rule                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Desired topology       | `alchemy.run.ts` and app build schemas                   | Local review records the exact commit                                                                               | Revert the repository commit; do not infer live state                                                                      |
| Alchemy state          | Read-only state-store receipt                            | Redacted, dated receipt under the approved reader                                                                   | Stop on a mismatch; state repair needs separate approval                                                                   |
| Cloudflare state       | Independent read-only provider receipt                   | Approved reader, redacted dated receipt                                                                             | Never substitute Alchemy state or old evidence                                                                             |
| Preview credentials    | Named Preview Environment mapping and `site/stg_preview` | Exact trusted PR head, quality result, Preview admission and environment-scoped Doppler bootstrap token             | Maps only Cloudflare account/token and Axiom token to the exact operation; any reviewer protection needs separate evidence |
| Production delivery    | Exact SHA, quality and Production approval               | Accepted main commit and Production Environment                                                                     | Use a new or reverted main commit for recovery; no direct rollback shortcut                                                |
| Direct Worker rollback | Approved break-glass record                              | Incident authority plus routes, bindings, assets, state, and provider reconciliation receipt                        | Prohibited by default under `SITE-D7`                                                                                      |
| DNS                    | Authoritative DNS/registrar readback                     | Current Production DNS/TLS/DNSSEC ownership is declared in Infrastructure; each mutation still needs exact approval | Unrelated DNS and registrar/account operations remain external; do not infer mutation authority                            |
| Observability          | Axiom datasets, logs, traces and metrics                 | Accepted Axiom-first policy, exact task/runbook authority, provider query report                                    | No initial alerts; no provider/ingestion claim without readback                                                            |
| Historical retention   | Dated receipts and evidence index                        | Preserved historical bytes; no current packet writer                                                                | Never retain raw provider bodies or secrets in Git                                                                         |

## Receipt minimum

Every run records the repository commit, target/stage, actor and authority
receipt, preflight results, exact operation or explicit no-op, postcondition,
rollback target, and limitation/non-claim. Omit secrets, raw provider bodies,
tenant identifiers, deployment identifiers, headers, and tokens. Retain a
failed or inconclusive receipt with its resume trigger; it is not evidence that
the target was changed.

The original HGI-111 deferred records remain represented by their immutable
dated acceptance receipt. Current policy is resolved by
[`HGI-104-decision-resolution.json`](../documentation-audit/HGI-104-decision-resolution.json).

The local Cloudflare command adapter keeps its complete sanitized diagnostic in
an ignored, SHA-addressed artifact with a 30-day operational target and prints
only a bounded receipt. HGI-108 does not implement automatic deletion; HGI-109
owns any retention-control admission.
Missing or corrupt local detail fails closed and must be repaired without
rerunning solely for diagnostics. This local adapter receipt is distinct from a
runbook's provider readback and never establishes a provider consequence.

The canonical journey IDs and current proof owners live in
[`../verification/README.md`](../verification/README.md). Historical packet
records and the retention index remain reachable there. Runbooks produce the
named evidence; they do not promote raw workflow artifacts into durable
identity.
Local documentation checks and dry runs establish only that the procedure is
findable and stops correctly. They do not prove a preview, production deploy,
credential rotation, provider state, DNS state, Axiom ingestion, artifact
retention, or rollback.

| ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Inventory and mutation preflight            | [inventory-and-preflight](cloudflare/inventory-and-preflight.md) | Redacted Executor Personal readback, discrepancy receipt, or inconclusive stop | Reader/query unavailable, target mismatch, or Alchemy/provider views disagree     |
| Preview lifecycle and orphan reconciliation | [preview-lifecycle](cloudflare/preview-lifecycle.md)             | Exact trusted PR head, one native `pr-<number>` deploy and exact-stage cleanup | Missing Preview admission, Doppler mapping, exact commit or cleanup authority     |
| Production delivery                         | [production-deploy](cloudflare/production-deploy.md)             | Exact accepted main SHA, one native `prod` deploy and Alchemy-owned resources  | Missing Production approval, exact commit or recovery identity                    |
| Credentials and remote state                | [credentials-and-state](cloudflare/credentials-and-state.md)     | Least-privilege, target-specific custody with fail-closed readback             | Issuer/custodian contract, revocation path, or exact external task is absent      |
| Incident recovery and rollback              | [incident-and-rollback](cloudflare/incident-and-rollback.md)     | Reverted main commit; Axiom-first investigation; DNS report-only               | Direct rollback, DNS mutation, or destructive observability action                |
| Axiom observability operations              | [site-axiom-observability](site-axiom-observability.md)          | Stage-isolated resource ownership and ordinary telemetry                       | Missing exact task authority, credential custody, provider readback, or ingestion |

## Authority and recovery matrix

| Boundary               | Source of truth                                          | Required approval/receipt                                                                                           | Recovery rule                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Desired topology       | `alchemy.run.ts` and app build schemas                   | Local review records the exact commit                                                                               | Revert the repository commit; do not infer live state                                                                      |
| Alchemy state          | Read-only state-store receipt                            | Redacted, dated receipt under the approved reader                                                                   | Stop on a mismatch; state repair needs separate approval                                                                   |
| Cloudflare state       | Independent read-only provider receipt                   | Approved reader, redacted dated receipt                                                                             | Never substitute Alchemy state or old evidence                                                                             |
| Preview credentials    | Named Preview Environment mapping and `site/stg_preview` | Exact trusted PR head, quality result, Preview admission and environment-scoped Doppler bootstrap token             | Maps only Cloudflare account/token and Axiom token to the exact operation; any reviewer protection needs separate evidence |
| Production delivery    | Exact SHA, quality and Production approval               | Accepted main commit and Production Environment                                                                     | Use a new or reverted main commit for recovery; no direct rollback shortcut                                                |
| Direct Worker rollback | Approved break-glass record                              | Incident authority plus routes, bindings, assets, state, and provider reconciliation receipt                        | Prohibited by default under `SITE-D7`                                                                                      |
| DNS                    | Authoritative DNS/registrar readback                     | Current Production DNS/TLS/DNSSEC ownership is declared in Infrastructure; each mutation still needs exact approval | Unrelated DNS and registrar/account operations remain external; do not infer mutation authority                            |
| Observability          | Axiom datasets, logs, traces and metrics                 | Accepted Axiom-first policy, exact task/runbook authority, provider query report                                    | No initial alerts; no provider/ingestion claim without readback                                                            |
| Historical retention   | Dated receipts and evidence index                        | Preserved historical bytes; no current packet writer                                                                | Never retain raw provider bodies or secrets in Git                                                                         |

## Receipt minimum

Every run records the repository commit, target/stage, actor and authority
receipt, preflight results, exact operation or explicit no-op, postcondition,
rollback target, and limitation/non-claim. Omit secrets, raw provider bodies,
tenant identifiers, deployment identifiers, headers, and tokens. Retain a
failed or inconclusive receipt with its resume trigger; it is not evidence that
the target was changed.

The original HGI-111 deferred records remain represented by their immutable
dated acceptance receipt. Current policy is resolved by
[`HGI-104-decision-resolution.json`](../documentation-audit/HGI-104-decision-resolution.json).

The local Cloudflare command adapter keeps its complete sanitized diagnostic in
an ignored, SHA-addressed artifact with a 30-day operational target and prints
only a bounded receipt. HGI-108 does not implement automatic deletion; HGI-109
owns any retention-control admission.
Missing or corrupt local detail fails closed and must be repaired without
rerunning solely for diagnostics. This local adapter receipt is distinct from a
runbook's provider readback and never establishes a provider consequence.

The canonical journey IDs and current proof owners live in
[`../verification/README.md`](../verification/README.md). Historical packet
records and the retention index remain reachable there. Runbooks produce the
named evidence; they do not promote raw workflow artifacts into durable
identity.
Local documentation checks and dry runs establish only that the procedure is
findable and stops correctly. They do not prove a preview, production deploy,
credential rotation, provider state, DNS state, Axiom ingestion, artifact
retention, or rollback.

# Deployment architecture

Alchemy owns deployment of Site's Cloudflare and Axiom resources. The GitHub
quality workflow checks out and tests one exact commit, then passes that SHA
to the delivery workflow. Delivery calls native Alchemy once.

## Preview

The [Preview workflow](../../.github/workflows/cloudflare-branch-preview.yml)
checks the live pull request, owner, repository, label and exact head before
fetching Preview credentials. It derives the stage as `pr-<number>`, rebuilds
the accepted checkout, checks generated assets and runs
`bun alchemy deploy --stage "pr-<number>" --yes`.

The [cleanup workflow](../../.github/workflows/cloudflare-branch-preview-cleanup.yml)
uses trusted default-branch code, checks the current pull request again, and
runs `bun alchemy destroy alchemy.destroy.ts --stage "pr-<number>" --yes`.
Shared Production datasets and dashboards are outside that stage.

## Production

The [Production workflow](../../.github/workflows/alchemy-main.yml) requires
`main`, the current GitHub SHA and the same SHA accepted by quality. It uses
the named Production Environment and runs
`bun alchemy deploy --stage prod --yes`.

Production deployment is supported through that workflow. There is no local
Production deploy wrapper. The root `production:plan` command remains an
optional native Alchemy diagnostic.

## Credentials and runtime telemetry

Doppler supplies `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and
`AXIOM_TOKEN` to the native Alchemy step through the matching GitHub
Environment. The workflow selects `ALCHEMY_PROFILE=site-ci-env-v1`; GitHub
provides non-interactive CI mode. Credentials are not printed or retained.

Alchemy still declares datasets, dashboards, tokens, destinations and metrics
secrets. The application still records ordinary request metrics, and Cloudflare
exports logs and traces. There are no special proof-marker requests or custom
post-deploy Cloudflare, public-route, dashboard or Axiom verification commands.

## Results and recovery

The native command's exit status determines delivery success or failure. Its
output remains in the ordinary workflow log. A successful command reports
Alchemy completion; it does not establish ongoing public availability or
telemetry ingestion.

Release tags and Changesets remain release metadata. Lighthouse, application
tests and browser checks remain part of local quality. Their results do not
claim a Production deployment.

Recover through a new or reverted exact commit and the same quality and Alchemy
workflow. Use [the incident runbook](../runbooks/cloudflare/incident-and-rollback.md)
for an incident. Provider repair, credential changes and resource teardown
remain separate operations. The native state entrypoint
[`alchemy.state.run.ts`](../../alchemy.state.run.ts) remains available for
authorised investigation.

The [Preview](../runbooks/cloudflare/preview-lifecycle.md) and
[Production](../runbooks/cloudflare/production-deploy.md) runbooks own the
operating steps.

| Direct Worker rollback | Approved break-glass record                              | Incident authority plus routes, bindings, assets, state, and provider reconciliation receipt                        | Prohibited by default under `SITE-D7`                                                                                      |
| DNS                    | Authoritative DNS/registrar readback                     | Current Production DNS/TLS/DNSSEC ownership is declared in Infrastructure; each mutation still needs exact approval | Unrelated DNS and registrar/account operations remain external; do not infer mutation authority                            |
| Observability          | Axiom datasets, logs, traces and metrics                 | Accepted Axiom-first policy, exact task/runbook authority, provider query report                                    | No initial alerts; no provider/ingestion claim without readback                                                            |
| Historical retention   | Dated receipts and evidence index                        | Preserved historical bytes; no current packet writer                                                                | Never retain raw provider bodies or secrets in Git                                                                         |

## Receipt minimum

Every run records the repository commit, target/stage, actor and authority
receipt, preflight results, exact operation or explicit no-op, postcondition,
rollback target, and limitation/non-claim. Omit secrets, raw provider bodies,
tenant identifiers, deployment identifiers, headers, and tokens. Retain a
failed or inconclusive receipt with its resume trigger; it is not evidence that
the target was changed.

The original HGI-111 deferred records remain represented by their immutable
dated acceptance receipt. Current policy is resolved by
[`HGI-104-decision-resolution.json`](../documentation-audit/HGI-104-decision-resolution.json).

The local Cloudflare command adapter keeps its complete sanitized diagnostic in
an ignored, SHA-addressed artifact with a 30-day operational target and prints
only a bounded receipt. HGI-108 does not implement automatic deletion; HGI-109
owns any retention-control admission.
Missing or corrupt local detail fails closed and must be repaired without
rerunning solely for diagnostics. This local adapter receipt is distinct from a
runbook's provider readback and never establishes a provider consequence.

The canonical journey IDs and current proof owners live in
[`../verification/README.md`](../verification/README.md). Historical packet
records and the retention index remain reachable there. Runbooks produce the
named evidence; they do not promote raw workflow artifacts into durable
identity.
Local documentation checks and dry runs establish only that the procedure is
findable and stops correctly. They do not prove a preview, production deploy,
credential rotation, provider state, DNS state, Axiom ingestion, artifact
retention, or rollback.

# Cloudflare incident recovery and rollback

This runbook owns Site incident classification, default recovery, and the
break-glass stop gate. It does not authorize access to Cloudflare, Alchemy, DNS,
credentials, logs, traces, or a deployed Worker.

## First response

1. Record the reporter, time, affected target, exact commit identity if known,
   observed symptom, and whether the report is local, hosted workflow, Alchemy,
   Cloudflare, DNS, public journey, or observability evidence.
2. Preserve only redacted, dated evidence. Classify unknown provider state as
   inconclusive rather than copying an old observation into current policy.
3. Use [inventory and preflight](inventory-and-preflight.md) before proposing
   any provider action. Stop if Alchemy and Cloudflare differ or the approved
   provider reader is unavailable.
4. Prefer a new or reverted main-branch commit through the complete delivery
   graph. Each production run still requires Cooper's approval for its exact
   main SHA and one workflow run under `SITE-D1`.

An HTML `200` with a failed referenced CSS, JavaScript, font, or image asset is

# Cloudflare incident recovery and rollback

This runbook owns Site incident classification, default recovery, and the
break-glass stop gate. It does not authorize access to Cloudflare, Alchemy, DNS,
credentials, logs, traces, or a deployed Worker.

## First response

1. Record the reporter, time, affected target, exact commit identity if known,
   observed symptom, and whether the report is local, hosted workflow, Alchemy,
   Cloudflare, DNS, public journey, or observability evidence.
2. Preserve only redacted, dated evidence. Classify unknown provider state as
   inconclusive rather than copying an old observation into current policy.
3. Use [inventory and preflight](inventory-and-preflight.md) before proposing
   any provider action. Stop if Alchemy and Cloudflare differ or the approved
   provider reader is unavailable.
4. Prefer a new or reverted main-branch commit through the complete delivery
   graph. Each production run still requires Cooper's approval for its exact
   main SHA and one workflow run under `SITE-D1`.

An HTML `200` with a failed referenced CSS, JavaScript, font, or image asset is
a public static-asset outage, not a healthy deployment. Record the HTML URL,
asset URL, status, redirect/location, content type, cache headers, and bounded
body evidence, then compare the exact deployed source/config identity with the
build-time asset proof. A reachable Worker or positive provider asset metadata
does not close this incident.

## Break-glass direct Worker rollback

`SITE-D7` accepts only a prohibition: direct Worker rollback is forbidden
unless a separate approved break-glass record names authority, preflight,
routes, bindings, assets, Alchemy and provider reconciliation, evidence,
revocation, rollback, and escalation. It is never sufficient to move a Worker
version and reconcile later.

Before any future direct rollback, the approved record must account for the
target version, public routes, Worker bindings, static assets, Alchemy remote
state, dependent preview stages, credential expiry/revocation, and independent
post-action Alchemy plus Cloudflare readback. If any item is unknown, stop and
escalate; no direct rollback occurs.

Production Axiom datasets are retained by default and are not part of an
ordinary Worker rollback. Any proposed dataset removal is a separate
destructive operation. Before approval, record the exact dataset names and
logical IDs, dependency and retention impact, secret-negative dry-plan digest,
recovery limits, and independent post-action Alchemy plus Axiom absence
readbacks. A missing item, foreign resource, replacement row, or unclear owner
stops the operation. This runbook does not grant that approval.

## DNS and observability boundaries

The historical `SITE-D8` exclusion does not describe the current declared
Production graph. The [Cloudflare architecture](../../architecture/cloudflare-alchemy-workers.md)
owns the current boundary: retained zone/TLS/DNSSEC plus Website-owned
apex/www DNS/TLS and tagged redirect; unrelated records and registrar/account
operations remain external. None of those declarations grants incident
mutation authority. Unexplained drift still stops for an exact owner and
approval; public DNS alone does not prove Alchemy ownership. `SITE-D9` permits only Cooper-owned manual read-only queries of
operational metadata, with compliance proved first. Never retain or query
secrets, bodies, cookies, authorization headers, sensitive query values, or
unrestricted attributes. Do not alert, spend, mutate configuration, or retain
provider operational data for more than 30 days; if compliance is unproved,
record inconclusive and stop.

## Receipt, recovery, and escalation

An incident receipt identifies the classification, last successful step,
observed state, target, authority status, redacted artifacts, default recovery
commit, blocked decision, escalation owner, and resume trigger. Retain
failed and inconclusive receipts. The rollback of this documentation slice is
to revert these runbooks; it does not alter infrastructure. This runbook does
not establish a live incident, provider state, DNS ownership, observability
availability, or rollback feasibility.

The receipt is indexed under the
[`Site verification route`](../../verification/README.md). Incident closure
requires same-commit post-action Alchemy/provider reconciliation and the
eleven named journeys; an HTTP recovery alone is not the rollback oracle.
